technology.heading: Calculated, not predicted
paragraphs: Your policy wording, catalogue or rulebook is configured into a deterministic decision tree. Given the facts of the case, the outcome is calculated from the wording. The same facts always give the same answer, and the answer can be explained clause by clause.

Agents do the reading. Photographs, PDFs, handwriting and emails become the facts the decision tree needs. Each agent does one small task, so a fault is easy to find and fix at the step where it happened.

faq.question: Is the outcome predicted by AI?
faq.answer: No. Your policy wording, catalogue or rules are turned into a decision tree. The amount is calculated from the facts, so the same facts always give the same answer.

faq.question: Where is AI used?
faq.answer: To read the claim. Agents turn photographs, PDFs, handwriting and emails into facts. Each agent is assigned one small task, so each step is clearly visible.

faq.question: Who makes the final decision?
faq.answer: Your team. By default, True Aim prepares a recommendation with full reasoning for a person to confirm. Full automation is available only where you and your regulator allow it.

faq.question: What happens when something is wrong?
faq.answer: Every assumption is on screen and can be changed. Every change records its reason. The fault is fixed at the step where it happened.

faq.question: Can we work from our own rules rather than the policy wording?
faq.answer: Yes. Industry catalogues and your own business rules work the same way as policy wording. One example is fair wear and tear rules for vehicles returned at the end of a lease.

faq.question: Which regulations is the record mapped against?
faq.answer: DORA, the EU AI Act and national rules including FINMA, BaFin, the NAIC and POPIA. The forensic view of the claim record shows every action by actor, so accountability is visible for every decision.

faq.question: Does it replace our claims system?
faq.answer: No. True Aim's Claims Decisioning works above the claims system you run, reads the claim from it and writes the recommendation back into it.

faq.question: What is the Decision Dossier?
faq.answer: The record of every decision: the inputs, the clauses applied, the calculation trace, the evidence links and who confirmed the outcome. It exports as one audit pack.

hero.title: Invoice Benchmarking: never overpay on an invoice again
hero.summary: Every invoice, quote and estimate is checked against the benchmark, by business line and by region. Your team sees which lines are too high, by how much and why, with the reissue request already drafted. Lower-value invoices no longer go unchecked, and every saving is recorded line by line.

unchecked.heading: Lower-value invoices no longer go unchecked
paragraphs: Most suppliers and trades publish no price list. Small invoices are either sent to an external assessor, which only pays off on large bills, or paid as they are.
A fixed fee per invoice makes it worth checking every invoice, including the small ones nobody opens today.

benchmark.heading: Our data, or an engine built from yours
paragraphs: Depending on your market, True Aim provides a proprietary benchmark from day one or builds a benchmark engine from your own data.
In Switzerland the benchmark draws on more than 100,000 property-claim invoices. In other markets True Aim builds it with local partners and from the data you already hold.
Either way, every line is tested against what the work should cost for that trade in that region. The benchmark keeps learning from the invoices you accept.

faq.question: Where does the price data come from?
faq.answer: In Switzerland, from more than 100,000 invoices from property claims, grouped by trade and by region. In other markets True Aim works with partners to build the benchmark from your own data.

faq.question: We only review invoices above a set amount. Why change?
faq.answer: Most overcharging sits below the threshold for external review. A fixed fee per invoice makes it worth checking the low-value invoices that nobody opens today.

faq.question: How do we see what it saves?
faq.answer: A dashboard shows how many invoices went through, how much was saved on each and what you paid for the platform. The return is visible at any time.

faq.question: Do we have to replace our claims system?
faq.answer: No. True Aim's Invoice Benchmarking works alongside the systems you already use and writes the adjusted amounts back into them.

cta.heading: Prove it on your own invoices

hero.summary: Produce a damage estimate and the full scope of work at first notification, from the photographs and documents your customer sends. Price the damage by region and list every trade and task in the order the work must run. Send assessors on site only where a visit changes the answer.

items.text: By WhatsApp, email, web form or phone. Missing items are flagged while the customer is still there.

items.title: 2. The damage is read

faq.question: Does True Aim replace our assessors?
faq.answer: No. True Aim's Damage Reporting gives your assessors an estimate and a scope on day one, with a note of what still needs checking in person. Site visits go where they change the answer.

faq.question: What does the customer need to send?
faq.answer: Photographs, any documents they have and a description in their own words. Details already on the policy are filled in for them.

faq.question: How is the estimate priced?
faq.answer: Against what each trade charges in that region, using the same benchmark data as True Aim's Invoice Benchmarking.

faq.question: Can True Aim start from an assessor's report?
faq.answer: Yes. A third-party report, cost estimate or appraisal can be the starting point. True Aim's Damage Reporting then works even where you do not run the customer journey yourself.

hero.title: Otus, True Aim's claims specialist
hero.summary: Otus is an AI-powered expert for every team member, in every True Aim solution. Ask Otus anything about a claim, by voice or text, and the answer comes from the claim, the policy and the record. Otus drafts, explains and plans, and has no decision rights: your team decides.

prompts.label: Otus: pick a scenario and see the answer
prompts.footer: No decision rights: Otus explains, drafts and plans. Your team decides.

items.prompt: Otus, I need to clear my backlog today. Where do I start?
answer: You have 14 open claims. Six are ready to confirm: the recommendation is complete and nothing is missing, about 20 minutes in total. Three are waiting on repairers, reminders went out at 08:30. Two need documents from the customer, chased this morning.
That leaves three for your judgment: 62850 (hotel nights above the cap), 64812 (disputed cause) and 64799 (two estimates far apart). Start with those three while you are fresh, then confirm the six.

items.prompt: Draft a handover email for claim 5964 to my colleague in property.
answer: Draft ready. Subject: Handover, claim 5964, motor warranty, J. Odermatt. What has happened: reported 3 October, five documents read, turbocharger and labour approved, oil and filter excluded under clause 2.4, courtesy vehicle set aside at the five-day cap.
What is open: the garage's revised invoice is due Friday. Next step: confirm the courtesy days once it is in. The full record is linked.

items.prompt: Why was line 4 on claim 62850 excluded? The customer is asking.
answer: Line 4 is the dishwasher replacement, 1'126.30. The policy covers the damage the water caused, not the appliance that caused it: clause 4.2, excluded causes. The invoice and the plumber's report both name the dishwasher as the source of the leak.
Here is a reply to the customer in plain language, quoting the clause. Nothing is sent until you send it.
